MEASURED 2026-08-12, twice in one session. `cap:degraded-surface` is VERIFIED and this does NOT falsify it — the capability did exactly what it promises. What this records is that its diagnosis CANNOT REACH a whole class of caller.

WHAT WAS OBSERVED: `tools/reflow2_cli.py` began answering `error: set_artifact_checksum: tool not found` for a tool that plainly exists and had worked minutes earlier. The natural reading is that the tool was renamed or removed. Both readings are wrong.

THE MECHANISM, traced rather than guessed. A `--serve-shared` daemon (pid 728580) held the store's write lock — confirmed with `fuser .reflow2/graph/LOCK`. A second server could not open the store, so it correctly served the DEGRADED SURFACE: a handshake plus exactly one tool, `reflow2_unavailable`, whose name is the diagnosis, with the translated reason in the server instructions, the remedies in the tool payload, and an explicit do-not-conclude-reflow2-is-missing. All of that was built, and all of it was present.

⇒ AND NONE OF IT WAS SEEN, because the caller never asked for it. The CLI goes straight to `tools/call` by NAME. rmcp's tool router then answers `invalid_params("tool not found")` — rmcp-2.2.0 `handler/server/router/tool.rs:567`, a generic string with no context, not reflow2's text at all. The CLI printed it faithfully. THE DIAGNOSIS LIVES IN THE HANDSHAKE AND THE TOOL LIST, AND A BY-NAME CALLER READS NEITHER.

So the careful part — "do not conclude reflow2 is missing" — was rendered as, precisely, "this tool does not exist". The capability's own stated purpose is that the server explains its own absence instead of vanishing; against a direct caller it vanishes.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE CLI: any client that caches a tool list, or that calls by name from a script, is in this class. The degraded surface is reachable only by a client that re-reads the surface after failing — which is the client least likely to be a script.

FIX DIRECTION, NOT DECIDED: the refusal for an unknown tool name is rmcp's, so reflow2 cannot reword it in place. Either the CLI re-reads `tools/list` on any `tool not found` and surfaces `reflow2_unavailable` if that is all there is, or the degraded server declines the call in a way that carries its own text. The first is cheap, local, and needs no upstream change.

NOTE ON THE LOCK ITSELF: this is NOT `fact:defect-rebuild-strands-the-shared-server`, which is a deleted-inode spawn failure. Different cause, and that one is fixed. This is ordinary single-writer contention behaving as designed, reported unrecognisably.
